note: POS Shopper Display: lead with the revenue angle
old:
A customer-facing display at every register.

Every register can run a second, customer-facing shopper display. It is a mode of the same POS app rather than a separate product, so the device running targeted video and brand-sponsored offers can switch to taking a checkout when the queue needs it.

  • A second screen the customer can see, running the same POS app in display mode
  • Customers enroll in loyalty themselves by scanning a QR code, no reading out an email address or phone number across the counter, which means fewer errors and a faster line
  • Targeted video ads and brand-sponsored offers at checkout
  • Included with every deployment, not a separate system to maintain
new:
The screen facing the customer is also ad space you can sell.

Every register can run a second, customer-facing shopper display. It is a mode of the same POS app rather than a separate product, so the device showing vendor-sponsored video can switch to taking a checkout when the queue needs it. What it shows is targeted using the customer profile and purchase history already on the POS, which is what makes the space worth paying for.

  • Vendors pay to run targeted video, product launches and coupons at the register, reaching the customer at the moment of purchase
  • Placement is priced against purchase history and customer profile, so a vendor is buying an audience rather than a screen
  • Competing brands can bid for the same customers, and the retailer sets the rate
  • Customers enroll in loyalty themselves by scanning a QR code, no reading out an email address or phone number across the counter
  • Included with every deployment, not a separate system to maintain
